1. Model consistently overestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes — reduce initial forecast values by 2–5% to align with observed mean reversion.

2. After a sharp price spike (e.g., >85), model tends to overshoot and then overcorrect — dampen forecast peaks by 5–10% and smooth transitions to avoid exaggerated declines.

3. Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast — adjust downward by 1–3% to reflect recent downward momentum or policy-induced cooling.

4. Forecast mean is typically 3–5% higher than true outcome — apply a global downward bias of 3–5% to all forecast values to correct for persistent overconfidence.

5. Model exhibits lagged response to price changes — if true price drops by >3% from prior day, reduce forecast by 1–2% for the next 3–5 days to reflect delayed reaction.
